newsitem.title: USA: "Star Wars" fends off volcano picture at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Star Wars" fends off volcano picture at U.S. box office.

text.p: "Star Wars" once again reigned at the U.S. box office during the weekend, easily fending off the high-profile launch of the volcano disaster movie "Dante's Peak," according to studio estimates released Sunday.
"Star Wars" earned $22.8 million during the Friday to Sunday period, while "Dante's Peak" opened in second with $18.6 million.

The two movies easily dominated the box office, making more than the rest of the top 10 combined. Opening in a distant third with $4.0 million was "The Beautician and the Beast," a comedy vehicle for Fran Drescher, star of television's "The Nanny."

In its second weekend of re-release, "Star Wars" averaged $10,822 from 2,104 screens. Its 10-day total stands at $69.2 million, taking its lifetime tally to $391.9 million. It has become the second highest-grossing movie at the domestic box office, and is poised to pass the $399.8 million record of the 1982 movie "E.T. The Extraterrestrial" next weekend. "Star Wars" is released by 20th Century Fox, a unit of News Corp. .

"Dante's Peak," with a production budget of about $115 million, stars Pierce Brosnan and Linda Hamilton who battle a volcano vn a Pacific Northwest town. Although it broke the February three-day record of $15.7 million reached in 1992 by "Wayne's World," critics were unimpressed. A Variety poll of critics in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago and Washington D.C. showed that five liked it, 18 did not and 16 were mixed.
Nonetheless, "Dante's Peak" averaged a strong $7,006 from 2,655 screens. The movie is released by Universal Pictures, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd..
Drescher's "The Beautician And The Beast," released by Viacom Inc. unit Paramount Pictures, averaged a meager $2,221 from 1,801 screens.

Last week's No. 2, "Jerry Maguire," slipped two places to fourth with $3.6 million. Its total now stands at $121.3 million. Also down two was "Scream," which was fifth with $3.5 million and a cumulative gross of $75 million.

Re-entering the top 10 was Oscar contender "The English Patient," which earned an estimated $2.2 million after boosting its screen total by 387 to 1,042, for an average of $2,111. The movie was eighth, up from 14 last weekend, and has now earned a total of $42 million.

The nominations for the 69th Academy Awards will be announced in Beverly Hills Tuesday. In addition to "The English Patient," there is a strong buzz for such movies as "Evita," "Fargo," "The People Vs. Larry Flynt" and "Shine."
